name: example-layout-composition
body:
Load-time example layout composition: the example check — templates-dir-validation step 7 — executes each template's layout against the library's layout set rather than that layout's text alone. A library layout's name is its layout file path: the layer root joined with the layout's path within its layer — `<layer root>/slides/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl` for a slide layout and `<layer root>/sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl` for a section layout, the name the loader builds (`path.Join(root, layoutRel)`, loadlibrary.go) and that render registers each layout under (`layoutName` / `namespaceForLayer`, render.go). Every layout text the merged library contributes — each slide layout and each section layout, whichever layer carries it — is parsed into one html/template namespace keyed by that layout name, so a layout's `{{ template "<layer root>/slides|sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl" . }}` call resolves the named library layout exactly as it resolves against the render-time shared namespace (template-language, library-layer-references). A two-layer library keys each layer's layouts under that layer's own root, so a layout in one layer invokes a layout in the other layer by the target's own root-qualified name (for example `{{ template "<external root>/sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl" . }}`). The namespace is built with the example-checked template's own function map and its own owning layer's `media` sub-filesystem, so every layout in the namespace — the example-checked layout itself and any layout it invokes with `{{ template }}` — resolves its `media` helper in the example-checked template's own owning layer, matching the render-time per-layer namespaces (namespaceForLayer, library-layer-references): html/template fixes the function set for the whole namespace when the namespace is parsed. The `section` helper is the load-time example helper — the re-parse override of the parse-resolvable `section` stub — so a `{{ section "<name>" }}` call renders its target at step 7 instead of failing, and the section target's own layout is re-parsed with the target's own owning layer's `media`, so the target's references resolve in the target's own layer. A `{{ template }}` call naming no library layout fails step 7 with a file:line-qualified templates error (template-language, templates-dir-validation). This holds for a single-layer library and for each layer of a two-layer library.

AC: a layout that invokes another library layout names it by the target's layout name, e.g. `{{ template "<layer root>/slides/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl" . }}`; the example check executes the invoked layout's markup at step 7; the named layout resolves whether it is a slide layout (`<layer root>/slides/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl`) or a section layout (`<layer root>/sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl`); in a two-layer library a local-layer layout resolves an external-layer layout by the external layer's own root-qualified name; the example-checked layout's own `{{ media "<path>" }}` and every `{{ media }}` in a layout it invokes with `{{ template }}` resolve in the example-checked template's own owning layer; a layout calling `{{ section "<name>" }}` executes its target at step 7 with the target's own owning layer's `media`; a `{{ template }}` call naming no library layout fails step 7 with a file:line-qualified templates error.
